outcome: No proof, disproof, or partial resolution of the stated conjecture (a bound N(K,g) on the number of K-rational points on any genus g≥2 curve over a number field K) was found in the window; all located post-2024-01-26 activity concerns distinct, differently-scoped conjectures that happen to share the name "uniform boundedness."
summary: The stated conjecture asks for a bound N(K,g) on the number of K-rational points on any genus g≥2 curve over a number field K, depending only on K and g, not on the curve's height, degree, or embedding. I searched extensively for anything bearing on this exact question since 26 January 2024 and found none. Several literature threads use the phrase 'uniform boundedness conjecture' or closely adjacent language but address genuinely different mathematical objects, per the scope rule of §3.1 (a related problem, not a case of this one): (1) the dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture of Morton-Silverman, about preperiodic/torsion points of rational maps or polynomial dynamical systems (arXiv:2105.05240 on polynomials over number fields, Doyle-Faber on rational maps with automorphisms arXiv:2401.11309, Doyle-Poonen work referenced in surveys, and follow-ups through 2025); (2) uniform boundedness of torsion/small points on abelian varieties over function fields, resolved in that function-field setting by Looper-Yap (March 2026, arXiv preprint) and related work by Gao — these concern abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0, not curves of genus g≥2 over number fields; (3) the 'dimension growth conjecture' / Bombieri-Pila-type bounds on rational points of height ≤ H on a curve of given degree, most recently sharpened by Binyamini-Cluckers-Kato (Proc. LMS 2025, arXiv:2401.03982, submitted 8 Jan 2024 — itself before the window) and by a 2024 IMRN paper of Binyamini-Cluckers-Novikov — these bound points by height and degree, not a height-independent bound depending only on genus and field, so they do not touch the stated conjecture even though they are much closer in spirit; (4) Bremner's conjecture on arithmetic progressions on elliptic curves (arXiv:2604.04850), which is about rank, not point-count uniformity for genus ≥2 curves. I also checked whether the conjecture has been formalized or attacked via proof assistants: a Google DeepMind formal-conjectures GitHub issue (#1820) proposes adding the exact statement to a Lean formalization corpus, but it is an open formalization request (labeled 'needs-prerequisites' and 'new conjecture'), not a proof of any kind, and involves no AI-generated mathematics — it is a request for a Mathlib-target statement. The Wikipedia article itself (checked directly) still lists the same partial results predating the window (Caporaso-Harris-Mazur 1997 conditional on Bombieri-Lang, Stoll's and Katz-Rabinoff-Zureick-Brown's work on the weaker Mazur Conjecture B, and the 2021 Dimitrov-Gao-Habegger resolution of Conjecture B) with nothing added since. No AI system was found anywhere near any of this work; the Doyle-Faber and Looper-Yap papers are ordinary human-authored proofs with no stated AI assistance.
competing_reading: One could argue the Binyamini-Cluckers-Kato dimension-growth bound is 'close enough' to count as progress, since uniform (in height) point-counts are the classical tool (Bombieri-Pila/Heath-Brown determinant method) used to attack uniform boundedness, and the sharpened d² factor is a genuine advance in that toolkit. But the bound is explicitly height-dependent (grows with H) and per-curve rather than uniform over all curves of a fixed genus, so under the stated question (a bound N(K,g) with no height parameter) it remains a related-but-distinct problem, consistent with the triage's judgment.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving, for some or all g≥2 and some class of number fields K, a bound on the total number of K-rational points on a genus-g curve that does not depend on the height, degree, or any other invariant of the specific curve beyond g and K itself — or a counterexample showing no such bound exists for some (K,g).
